headline: Sensex and Nifty Give Up Early Gains to Close Lower as Banking Drag and Oil Surge Offset IT Gains

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Early rally fizzled out as banking stocks dragged down the market benchmark indices.
A surge in global crude oil prices triggered selling pressure across key sectors.
Markets closed lower for the second straight session after slumping over 900 points from day highs.
Persistent selling pressure offset gains seen in IT sector stocks.
whatHappening: Sensex declined 143.21 points to settle at 73,709.69, while Nifty dropped to 22,811.35.
IT stocks shined and led early market gains before broader selling took over.
Persistent Systems launched a Rs 4,265-crore QIP with a floor price of Rs 5,550 per share.
FSSAI pulled up Nestlé India seeking scientific proof over product digestive claims.
summary: Indian equity markets opened higher on strong IT cues but erased gains to close lower for the second straight session on October 21. Pressure from banking stocks and rising crude oil prices pulled Sensex down 143 points to 73,709.69, while Nifty settled near 22,811. Persistent Systems made news with its QIP launch, while Nestlé India faced regulatory scrutiny from FSSAI.
